assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is LLM-as-judge evaluation, pairwise/pointwise scoring, Elo/arena ranking, bias calibration, and human spot-check loops
evaluation is model-graded unless human annotation is explicitly configured
candidate model outputs are already generated; generation infrastructure is out of scope
exclusions: dataset curation and data collection beyond evaluation sets
downstream product decisions beyond evaluation reporting

competency_questions.question: What evaluation paradigm (pointwise/pairwise/listwise) is used and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JUDGE_PARADIGM, POINTWISE, PAIRWISE define paradigm and selection rationale

competency_questions.question: How is the LLM judge validated against human preferences before deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUMAN_CALIBRATION and JUDGE_MODEL_SELECT define validation protocol

competency_questions.question: What rubric dimensions and grade anchors are used for pointwise scoring?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RUBRIC_DESIGN and POINTWISE define scoring dimensions

competency_questions.question: How is position bias detected and corrected in pairwise evaluation?
How are Elo ratings computed and when are they considered stable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELO_ARENA defines rating update and CI stability criteria

competency_questions.question: How are verbosity and position biases measured and mitigated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERBOSITY_BIAS and POSITION_BIAS define measurement and mitigation

competency_questions.question: How is self-preference bias detected when judge and candidate share a model family?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_PREF defines detection method and mitigation via judge diversity

competency_questions.question: How are human spot-checks integrated to prevent silent judge drift?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HUMAN_CALIBRATION defines sampling strategy and drift alert protocol

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination detected before evaluating a new model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_CONTAM defines n-gram overlap and canary probing

competency_questions.question: What monitoring is in place to detect Goodhart's Law gaming of the judge metric?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART and HUMAN_CALIBRATION define monitoring and alert criteria

competency_questions.question: How is evaluation cost managed without sacrificing ranking reliability?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_LATENCY and EVAL_PIPELINE define tiering and sampling strategy

competency_questions.question: How are safety and helpfulness jointly evaluated to avoid over-refusal masking?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAFETY_EVAL and MULTI_DIM_SCORING define dual-threshold evaluation

competency_questions.question: How are evaluation results communicated with appropriate uncertainty quantification?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAL_REPORTING defines CI inclusion and limitations disclosure

glossary.definition: scoring each output independently on an absolute rubric without cross-output comparison
comparing two outputs and eliciting a preference verdict or tie
continuous skill rating derived from pairwise match outcomes via the Elo update formula
judge tendency to favor the first or last presented option in pairwise comparison regardless of quality
judge tendency to prefer longer more elaborate responses independent of actual quality
tendency of a judge model to rate outputs from models with similar training or its own outputs higher
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; metric gaming degrades proxy validity
evaluation inflation when test questions appear in candidate model training data
rate at which pairwise verdicts remain consistent when A/B order is swapped
degree of agreement between independent annotators or judges measured by Cohen kappa or Krippendorff alpha

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for LLM-as-judge evaluation work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Zheng et al. 2023 (MT-Bench/LLM-as-a-Judge) and Chiang et al. 2024 (Chatbot Arena) conceptually but not as observed evidence
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Zheng et al. 2023 arXiv:2306.05685; Chiang et al. 2024 arXiv:2403.04132

nodes.definition: Establish the LLM-as-judge paradigm: use a capable language model to evaluate free-form outputs via pointwise, pairwise, or listwise prompts, replacing expensive human annotation at scale.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new judge model released or human calibration data collected

pros.claim: Scales to millions of outputs without human annotators
pros.example: GPT-4-as-judge evaluates 10k chatbot responses overnight

cons.claim: Judge bias and self-preference corrupt results if uncalibrated
cons.example: GPT-4 rates GPT-4 outputs 10-15% higher than human consensus

failure_modes: position bias flips pairwise verdicts
verbosity bias favors longer responses
self-preference if judge==candidate
acceptance_tests: judge agreement with human annotations >0.80 Pearson on held-out set
position-swap consistency rate >0.85

nodes.definition: Score each candidate output independently on a numeric rubric (e.g., 1-5 Likert), yielding absolute quality estimates without cross-candidate comparison.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rubric redesigned or task domain changes

pros.claim: Produces absolute scores enabling longitudinal comparison
pros.example: compare model v1 vs v2 without re-evaluating all pairs

cons.claim: High variance on subjective tasks; anchoring effects inflate scores
cons.example: all models cluster near 4/5 on open-ended generation

failure_modes: score bunching at top
rubric ambiguity yields low inter-rater agreement
no contrast between mediocre and good
acceptance_tests: score variance >0.5 across quality levels
rubric examples cover each grade level

nodes.definition: Present two candidate outputs to the judge and elicit a preference or tie verdict, building a partial order that aggregates into win rates.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: position bias audit fails or arena protocol changes

pros.claim: Higher inter-rater agreement than absolute scoring on subjective tasks
pros.example: arena human votes show 0.85+ agreement on pairwise vs 0.60 on 5-point scale

cons.claim: O(n^2) pairs for n models; position bias inflates first-presented option
cons.example: 100-model evaluation needs 4950 pairs × swap = 9900 calls

failure_modes: position bias: first option wins 55-60% without swap
verdict non-transitivity in three-way comparisons
acceptance_tests: swap-consistency rate >0.82
tie rate <25% on clearly differentiated outputs

nodes.definition: Aggregate pairwise match outcomes into a continuous skill rating (Elo/Bradley-Terry) for ranking models on an open arena platform.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: models updated or match volume crosses stability threshold

pros.claim: Handles intransitive preferences gracefully via probabilistic model
pros.example: Chatbot Arena ranks 50+ models with overlapping confidence intervals

cons.claim: Requires thousands of matches for stable rating; cold-start for new models
cons.example: new model needs 500+ matches to narrow CI below 30 Elo points

failure_modes: non-stationarity: model updates invalidate historical matches
category conflation across task types
adversarial match selection
acceptance_tests: 95% CI width <50 Elo points after 1000 matches
rank order stable across bootstrap resamples
revisit_triggers: match distribution skewed to easy queries

nodes.definition: Design criterion-specific rubrics that operationalize quality dimensions (accuracy, coherence, safety, instruction-following) into scorable anchors for judge prompts.
inputs: sample outputs at each quality level

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task redesign or human calibration reveals rubric gaps

pros.claim: Explicit anchors reduce inter-rater variance and guide judge reasoning
pros.example: MT-Bench rubrics with reference answers cut score variance 30%

cons.claim: Rubric creation requires domain expert time and iterative refinement
cons.example: designing 8-dimension coding rubric takes 2-4 weeks with expert review

failure_modes: over-specific rubrics fail on out-of-distribution outputs
anchors unrepresentative of real quality levels
dimension overlap causes double-counting
acceptance_tests: inter-rater agreement >0.75 Cohen kappa on rubric pilot
every grade level has at least 2 anchor examples

nodes.definition: Detect and correct positional ordering effects in pairwise judge prompts where the judge systematically favors the first or second presented option.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: audit detects position skew or judge model changes

pros.claim: Swap augmentation halves position bias at cost of 2x judge calls
pros.example: Zheng et al. 2023: swap reduces inconsistency rate from 25% to 12%

cons.claim: 2x call overhead; inconsistent pairs must be handled as ties or discarded
cons.example: borderline cases become ties, reducing discriminative power

failure_modes: only swapping without checking consistency
ignoring format differences that confound position
acceptance_tests: swap-consistency rate >0.85 on pilot set
first-position win rate within [0.45,0.55]
bias audit report generated before large-scale evaluation begins

nodes.definition: Identify and mitigate the tendency of LLM judges to prefer longer, more elaborate responses independent of actual quality.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task type changes or length distribution shifts

pros.claim: Length-stratified analysis reveals whether bias exists before it corrupts leaderboard
pros.example: correlation plot of length vs win-rate exposes systematic preference

cons.claim: Controlling for length may suppress legitimate quality signal in verbose tasks
cons.example: in long-form writing, length can correlate with completeness

failure_modes: conflating verbosity with completeness
length normalization over-penalizing necessary detail
acceptance_tests: Spearman correlation of response length vs judge score <0.30 after debiasing
length-stratified win rates within 5% of mean
revisit_triggers: new task type with different length norms

nodes.definition: Measure and control the tendency of a judge model to rate outputs from models with similar training or its own outputs higher than objectively warranted.
inputs: pairwise verdicts segmented by judge-vs-candidate model family

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge or candidate model families updated or mixed

pros.claim: Using multiple judges from different families averages out self-preference
pros.example: 3-judge ensemble from different providers reduces self-pref delta to <3%

cons.claim: Multi-judge ensemble triples evaluation cost and requires aggregation protocol
cons.example: majority vote on disagreements adds latency and complexity

failure_modes: using single proprietary judge to evaluate competing proprietary models
ignoring training data overlap as a confounder
acceptance_tests: self-preference delta <5% relative to cross-family judge baseline
ensemble judge agreement >0.80 on calibration set
revisit_triggers: new model family added to evaluation
human calibration study reveals systematic bias

nodes.definition: Run periodic human annotation batches to calibrate LLM judge scores, detect drift, and validate that automated scores remain aligned with human preferences.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge model updated or agreement metric drops

pros.claim: Catches silent judge drift before it corrupts production metrics
pros.example: monthly 200-sample audit detected GPT-4 scoring shift after provider update

cons.claim: Human annotation is slow and expensive; sampling may miss tail failures
cons.example: 200-sample audit at $2/task = $400 + analyst time per cycle

failure_modes: sampling only easy cases, missing edge-case drift
using same annotators who designed rubrics, creating confirmation bias
acceptance_tests: human-judge Pearson correlation >0.80 on calibration sample
audit cycle completed before major evaluation report

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate contamination where candidate models have seen benchmark test questions during training, invalidating performance estimates.
inputs: model outputs on verbatim vs paraphrased prompts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new training run or benchmark published publicly

pros.claim: N-gram overlap detection flags obvious memorization before evaluation
pros.example: 8-gram overlap >50% on test questions signals contamination

cons.claim: Semantic contamination not caught by n-gram overlap; rephrasing hides it
cons.example: paraphrased benchmark items undetected by string matching

failure_modes: relying solely on string match, missing semantic contamination
not rotating benchmarks as training data expands
acceptance_tests: n-gram overlap <5% on final test set
canary probe accuracy not significantly above random baseline

nodes.definition: Monitor for and mitigate Goodhart's Law effects where optimizing the judge score becomes the goal, causing models to game the metric rather than improve genuine quality.

included: proxy metric vs true objective divergence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training objective changes to include judge score or human audit reveals gaming

pros.claim: Tracking multiple uncorrelated metrics makes gaming harder
pros.example: combining judge score, ROUGE, human rating, and task accuracy

cons.claim: Diversifying metrics complicates optimization and stakeholder communication
cons.example: teams disagree on which metric to optimize when they diverge

failure_modes: single judge score as sole training signal
judge and candidate from same family enabling style transfer
acceptance_tests: human quality tracks judge score within 10% over 3 evaluation cycles
metric divergence alert triggers when human-judge gap >0.15
revisit_triggers: model explicitly trained on judge scores
judge score trends diverge from human ratings

nodes.definition: Apply the MT-Bench framework (Zheng et al. 2023) for multi-turn instruction-following evaluation using GPT-4 as judge on 80 curated questions across 8 categories.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: MT-Bench questions become public or score saturation detected

pros.claim: Multi-turn design reveals instruction-following degradation invisible in single-turn evals
pros.example: turn-2 score drop >1 point flags context-forgetting models

cons.claim: Fixed 80-question set ages quickly; GPT-4 judge cost limits adoption
cons.example: $80+ per full evaluation run limits iteration speed

failure_modes: saturating upper bound as models improve
category imbalance masking weak dimensions
acceptance_tests: per-category variance documented
reference answers validated by domain expert

nodes.definition: Operate a live human-preference arena (Chiang et al. 2024) where users submit queries and vote on anonymous model outputs, producing crowd-sourced Elo rankings.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: voting anomalies detected or arena scope changes

pros.claim: Real user queries avoid benchmark contamination; crowd wisdom aggregates diverse preferences
pros.example: Chatbot Arena 1M+ votes provide near-oracle ranking signal

cons.claim: Volunteer bias skews toward tech-savvy English queries; adversarial voting possible
cons.example: underrepresents non-English, domain-expert, and safety-relevant queries

failure_modes: strategic voting by model developers
query distribution mismatch with target use case
acceptance_tests: vote authenticity checks in place
query distribution audit matches target demographic

nodes.definition: Select and validate the judge model considering capability, cost, self-preference risk, API reliability, and alignment with human preferences for the target domain.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge model deprecated or human alignment study completed

pros.claim: Validated judge selection prevents systematic bias before expensive evaluation runs
pros.example: pre-validation on 100-sample pilot saves downstream rerun cost

cons.claim: Smaller faster judges save cost but may miss subtle quality differences
cons.example: using Claude-Haiku as judge misses nuanced factual errors caught by Opus

failure_modes: selecting judge without domain alignment check
using same provider as candidate for cost savings
acceptance_tests: judge-human correlation >0.80 on domain pilot set
cost per evaluation within budget
self-preference delta <5% validated before deployment

nodes.definition: Prompt the judge model to produce explicit step-by-step reasoning before the verdict, improving consistency and enabling human audit of judge rationale.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge model updated or rationale quality drops

pros.claim: CoT reasoning reduces judge score variance and enables auditing
pros.example: rationale-before-verdict reduces score variance by ~0.3 on 1-10 scale

cons.claim: Longer prompts increase latency and token cost; rationale can post-hoc justify wrong verdicts
cons.example: CoT adds 2-3x token cost per judgment

failure_modes: reasoning disconnected from final verdict
judge fabricates plausible-sounding but wrong rationale
acceptance_tests: rationale cites specific output elements
verdict consistent with rationale direction >0.90

nodes.definition: Choose and implement reference-based (ground-truth comparison) versus reference-free (criteria-only) judge evaluation, managing tradeoffs in cost, coverage, and judge capability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task domain shifts or ground truth availability changes

pros.claim: Reference answers anchor judge scores for factual tasks, reducing hallucination tolerance
pros.example: math/coding tasks with reference answers catch subtle errors judges miss without ground truth

cons.claim: Reference construction is expensive and may introduce author bias
cons.example: writing reference answers for 500 open-ended questions requires 50+ expert hours

failure_modes: using reference-based eval for creative tasks where multiple valid answers exist
stale references for time-sensitive factual questions
acceptance_tests: reference answers validated by independent domain expert
reference-free and reference-based scores agree within 0.5 on calibration set

nodes.definition: Define multiple quality dimensions (accuracy, helpfulness, safety, coherence), score each independently, and aggregate via weighted combination for holistic model assessment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: dimension weights revised or new quality requirement added

pros.claim: Dimension separation reveals specific failure modes and guides targeted improvement
pros.example: separating safety from helpfulness allows focused fine-tuning per dimension

cons.claim: Weight choice is subjective and context-dependent; stakeholders disagree
cons.example: safety-vs-helpfulness weight debate delays evaluation finalization

failure_modes: high dimension correlation makes separate scores redundant
aggregation weights not documented leading to irreproducibility
acceptance_tests: inter-dimension correlation <0.70 across all pairs
weight rationale documented and stakeholder-approved

nodes.definition: Evaluate model outputs for harmful content, refusal appropriateness, jailbreak resistance, and alignment with safety policies using specialized safety judges and red-teaming.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: policy change or new harm category identified

pros.claim: Specialized safety judges outperform general judges on harm detection
pros.example: fine-tuned safety classifiers achieve 0.92+ F1 vs 0.70 for general judge on harm detection

cons.claim: Safety evaluation arms race: red-team prompts become public, enabling adversarial tuning
cons.example: published jailbreaks quickly become training signal for gaming

failure_modes: using general judge for harm detection below capability threshold
over-refusal inflating safety score while harming helpfulness
acceptance_tests: false negative rate on known harm categories <2%
over-refusal rate on benign inputs <5%

nodes.definition: Balance evaluation thoroughness against API cost and latency by selecting judge model tier, batching, caching, and sampling strategies.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: API pricing changes or volume spike

pros.claim: Stratified sampling with 30% of full set achieves 95% of ranking signal at 30% cost
pros.example: early stopping when Elo CI stabilizes saves 40% of arena compute

cons.claim: Aggressive sampling misses tail failures on rare but high-risk query types
cons.example: 10% sample misses 0.5% harm rate failures that matter for safety

failure_modes: caching stale judge outputs after model update
over-sampling easy queries that add no discriminative value
acceptance_tests: sampled evaluation reproduces full-set ranking within 2 Elo points
cost per evaluation cycle within approved budget

nodes.definition: Build and maintain the automated evaluation pipeline: prompt construction, judge API calls, result parsing, debiasing, aggregation, and reporting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: judge API changes or pipeline reproducibility check fails

pros.claim: Automated pipeline enables daily evaluation enabling rapid model iteration
pros.example: daily eval runs catch regressions within 24h of model update

cons.claim: Pipeline complexity creates silent failure modes: stale caches, prompt version drift
cons.example: wrong prompt template version used for 2 weeks before audit caught it

failure_modes: prompt version mismatch across runs
result aggregation bug inflating scores
retry logic masking judge errors
acceptance_tests: pipeline reproduces reference scores within 0.1 on fixed eval set
prompt version logged and validated per run

nodes.definition: Design evaluation protocols for specialized domains (coding, math, medical, legal) requiring domain-expert judges, domain-specific rubrics, and reference solutions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain standards change or expert agreement drops

pros.claim: Functional correctness testing for coding/math removes judge subjectivity entirely
pros.example: unit test pass rate is ground truth for code generation quality

cons.claim: Domain expert availability limits scalability; expert disagreement on edge cases
cons.example: hiring medical domain evaluators for clinical NLP costs 5-10x general annotation

failure_modes: using general rubric for domain-specific task where criteria don't apply
ground truth solutions contain errors propagated to evaluation
acceptance_tests: domain expert validates rubric against 20 real task examples
functional test suite achieves >95% coverage of acceptance criteria
revisit_triggers: new task type added to domain

nodes.definition: Measure and improve agreement between multiple human annotators or judge instances using Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha, and disagreement analysis.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: annotator cohort changes or rubric revised

pros.claim: Kappa-driven guideline revision cycles improve agreement from 0.55 to 0.80 within 3 rounds
pros.example: iterative calibration is fastest path to reliable labels

cons.claim: High agreement can mask systematic shared bias if all annotators share background
cons.example: all annotators from same culture may agree on culturally biased verdicts

failure_modes: treating high agreement as ground truth without diversity check
conflating chance agreement with genuine reliability
acceptance_tests: Cohen kappa >0.70 on pilot annotation batch
disagreement rate on clear cases <5%

nodes.definition: Produce structured evaluation reports with confidence intervals, limitations, and actionable findings for engineering, product, and leadership stakeholders.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reporting format requirements change or CI methodology updated

pros.claim: Confidence intervals and limitations prevent overinterpretation of small score differences
pros.example: reporting CI prevents spurious model selection based on noise

cons.claim: Stakeholders ignore nuanced limitations and treat point estimates as ground truth
cons.example: 'Model A scores 4.2 vs 4.1' decision ignores overlapping CIs

failure_modes: suppressing limitations to satisfy stakeholder narrative
omitting CI from reports to appear decisive
acceptance_tests: every score includes 95% CI
limitations section present and peer-reviewed

edges.resolution_rule: use MT-Bench for controlled multi-turn assessment and Arena for live user preference; do not substitute one for the other
low inter-rater agreement drives rubric revision; iterate rubric before scaling annotation
self-preference is an inherent risk of the judge paradigm; mitigate via judge diversity and human calibration

conflict_axes.description: Judge evaluation thoroughness (strong model, CoT, swap, multi-judge) increases cost and latency in direct proportion to quality gains.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use strongest judge for high-stakes evals; tiered model for rapid iteration; cache deterministic outputs.

conflict_axes.description: Automated LLM judge scales cheaply but drifts; human evaluation is ground truth but slow and expensive.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Automate at scale with periodic human spot-check calibration; trigger full human re-eval when drift detected.

conflict_axes.description: Most capable judges tend to share training distribution with candidates, amplifying self-preference bias.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Ensemble judges from multiple providers; report self-preference delta alongside scores.

conflict_axes.description: Static benchmarks enable controlled comparison but contaminate over time; live arenas avoid contamination but have volunteer bias.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use static benchmark for controlled ablation; arena for community trust; rotate benchmark questions annually.

conflict_axes.description: Pointwise enables absolute comparison across time; pairwise has higher agreement but O(n^2) cost and position bias.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Default to pairwise with swap for preference tasks; use pointwise for longitudinal tracking and regression detection.

conflict_axes.description: Reference-based evaluation is more reliable for factual tasks but expensive to construct; reference-free scales but misses subtle errors.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use reference-based for factual/coding tasks; reference-free for open-ended creative or conversational tasks.

conflict_axes.description: Any judge metric used as a training signal risks Goodhart's Law gaming, degrading its validity as a quality proxy.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Never use a single judge score as the sole training signal; maintain uncorrelated human evaluation as ground truth anchor.

conflict_axes.description: Maximizing safety scores tends to increase over-refusal, reducing helpfulness scores; joint optimization is required.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Score safety and helpfulness independently; require both to meet floor thresholds before aggregation.

conflict_axes.description: Fast evaluation (small samples, weak judge, no CoT) enables rapid iteration but produces noisy rankings with wide confidence intervals.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Run fast eval for internal iteration; full stable eval before external reporting or model release decisions.

conflict_axes.description: General evaluation metrics miss domain-specific quality criteria; domain-specific evals are more accurate but less transferable.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use general eval as baseline; supplement with domain-specific functional tests for high-stakes domain deployments.

edge_cases.scenario: Instruction-tuned judge evaluating outputs from same base model
edge_cases.trigger: judge and candidate share base model weights
edge_cases.risk: self-preference inflates scores by 10-20%, invalidating comparison
edge_cases.mitigation: Use judge from different provider family; report self-preference delta

edge_cases.scenario: Benchmark questions appear verbatim in candidate training data
edge_cases.trigger: evaluation dataset published online prior to model training cutoff
edge_cases.risk: inflated scores do not reflect generalization; ranking corruption
edge_cases.mitigation: N-gram overlap detection; canary probing; hold-out questions never published

edge_cases.scenario: Judge model updated by provider mid-evaluation campaign
edge_cases.trigger: provider silently updates judge model API endpoint
edge_cases.risk: score distribution shifts, making pre- and post-update results incomparable
edge_cases.mitigation: Pin judge model version; validate on fixed calibration set before each run

edge_cases.scenario: All outputs cluster at top of Likert scale (score bunching)
edge_cases.trigger: strong models all score 4.5-5.0 on 5-point rubric
edge_cases.risk: insufficient discrimination to rank models or detect regressions
edge_cases.mitigation: Switch to pairwise comparison or extend scale to 10-point

edge_cases.trigger: model developer or competitor submits strategic votes to manipulate leaderboard
edge_cases.risk: Elo ratings reflect gaming rather than quality
edge_cases.mitigation: Anomaly detection on voting patterns; IP deduplication; rate limiting

edge_cases.scenario: Model trained explicitly to maximize judge score
edge_cases.trigger: RLHF reward model is the same model used as evaluation judge
edge_cases.risk: Goodhart's Law: model games judge scoring style without quality improvement
edge_cases.mitigation: Rotate judge model; maintain separate held-out human evaluation

edge_cases.scenario: Safety over-refusal masking as high safety score
edge_cases.trigger: model refuses most borderline queries; safety judge rewards refusals
edge_cases.risk: model appears safe but is unhelpful; helpfulness blindspot in evaluation
edge_cases.mitigation: Measure both harm rate and over-refusal rate; require both to meet thresholds

edge_cases.scenario: Low inter-annotator agreement due to ambiguous rubric
edge_cases.trigger: new annotator cohort achieves kappa < 0.50 on pilot
edge_cases.risk: labels too noisy to train on or use as evaluation ground truth
edge_cases.mitigation: Pause annotation; revise rubric with disagreement examples; re-pilot

edge_cases.scenario: Domain expert judges disagree on correct answer
edge_cases.trigger: medical or legal task with genuine expert disagreement
edge_cases.risk: ground truth labels are unreliable; evaluation conclusions overstated
edge_cases.mitigation: Recruit 3+ domain experts; report disagreement rate; avoid binary labels on contested cases

edge_cases.scenario: Verbosity bias dominates pairwise win rate
edge_cases.trigger: longer outputs win 70%+ of pairwise matches irrespective of quality
edge_cases.risk: models optimize output length rather than quality
edge_cases.mitigation: Length-controlled pairwise; length-stratified win rate reporting

edge_cases.scenario: Cold-start model in arena with insufficient matches
edge_cases.trigger: new model enters arena with fewer than 200 matches
edge_cases.risk: Elo CI too wide to draw ranking conclusions; early match order has outsized effect
edge_cases.mitigation: Warm-start with 100+ seeded matches before public leaderboard listing; report CI width

edge_cases.trigger: evaluating outputs in low-resource language with English-pretrained judge
edge_cases.risk: judge capability degrades; quality differences not detected
edge_cases.mitigation: Use multilingual judge or native-speaker human evaluation for low-resource languages

workflow.action: Define evaluation goals and stakeholder requirements
Design evaluation mode (pointwise/pairwise) and debiasing strategy

workflow.gate: all bias metrics within acceptable bounds

workflow.action: Run contamination check on evaluation dataset
workflow.gate: n-gram overlap <5% on final test set
all candidates evaluated; no pipeline errors

workflow.action: Aggregate scores, compute Elo/win rates, run statistical analysis
Monitor for Goodhart gaming and schedule next calibration

dominance_rules.rule: Bias audit must precede large-scale evaluation
dominance_rules.condition: any pairwise or pointwise evaluation at scale
dominance_rules.rationale: Undetected bias invalidates all downstream scores; audit first is non-negotiable

dominance_rules.rule: Human calibration gates evaluation report publication
dominance_rules.condition: evaluation report intended for external audience or model release decision
dominance_rules.rationale: Without human ground-truth anchor, automated scores may reflect drift rather than quality

dominance_rules.condition: evaluating a newly trained model on any benchmark
dominance_rules.rationale: Contaminated scores are invalid; check first prevents wasted evaluation compute

dominance_rules.rule: Rubric design precedes pointwise and multi-dimensional scoring
dominance_rules.rationale: Scoring without defined rubric produces unreliable and non-reproducible results

dominance_rules.rule: Judge model selection must include self-preference audit
dominance_rules.condition: judge and candidate from same provider or base model family
dominance_rules.rationale: Self-preference bias of 10-20% renders single-family judge comparison invalid

dominance_rules.rule: Safety evaluation requires specialized safety judge, not general judge
dominance_rules.condition: evaluation includes harm, refusal, or jailbreak assessment
dominance_rules.rationale: General judges miss subtle harm patterns; false negative rate unacceptably high for safety-critical use

dominance_rules.rule: Goodhart monitoring must activate before using judge scores as training signal
dominance_rules.condition: judge scores fed into any reward model or RLHF loop
dominance_rules.rationale: Without monitoring, Goodhart gaming degrades model quality while inflating scores

dominance_rules.rule: Inter-rater agreement must reach kappa >0.70 before scaling annotation
dominance_rules.condition: human annotation for evaluation label collection
dominance_rules.rationale: Low-agreement labels add noise; scaling before threshold wastes budget and corrupts labels

dominance_rules.rule: Domain-specific evaluation required for high-stakes domain deployments
dominance_rules.condition: model deployed in medical, legal, or safety-critical domain
dominance_rules.rationale: General evaluation misses domain-specific failure modes that matter most for deployment risk

dominance_rules.rule: Reference-based evaluation preferred for factual and coding tasks
dominance_rules.condition: task has objectively correct or verifiable answers
dominance_rules.rationale: Reference-free evaluation of factual tasks misses subtle errors that domain experts catch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not redesign rubric after large-scale annotation has begun
anti_rework_rules.prevention: pilot with 50 samples and achieve kappa >0.70 before scaling
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: all collected labels must be re-annotated at full cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change judge model mid-evaluation campaign without version locking
anti_rework_rules.trigger: provider releases updated model during campaign
anti_rework_rules.prevention: pin model version at campaign start; validate on calibration set each run
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: pre/post results incomparable; full re-evaluation required

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not publish benchmark questions before model training cutoff
anti_rework_rules.prevention: hold evaluation questions under embargo until after training cutoff
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: contamination invalidates all future evaluations on that benchmark

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip swap augmentation in pairwise evaluation
anti_rework_rules.trigger: cost pressure to halve pairwise API calls
anti_rework_rules.prevention: build swap augmentation into pipeline default; require explicit override to disable
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: position bias corrupts win rates; retrospective debiasing is lossy

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not use judge scores as sole training reward without human calibration
anti_rework_rules.trigger: reward model trained directly on judge verdicts
anti_rework_rules.prevention: require human calibration report before judge scores enter any training loop
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: Goodhart gaming degrades model quality while inflating scores

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not aggregate multi-dimensional scores before validating dimension independence
anti_rework_rules.trigger: stakeholder requests single aggregate score before correlation analysis
anti_rework_rules.prevention: compute and report dimension correlations before weighting; flag correlated dimensions
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: correlated dimensions double-count; aggregate scores mislead model selection

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not launch arena before adversarial voting detection is operational
anti_rework_rules.prevention: implement vote anomaly detection before public launch
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: strategic voting corrupts Elo; retroactive correction requires full re-computation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip contamination check for newly trained models
anti_rework_rules.trigger: fast iteration culture skipping pre-eval checks
anti_rework_rules.prevention: contamination check is mandatory pipeline step before any benchmark evaluation
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: inflated scores invalidate release decision; public credibility damage if discovered post-release

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not omit confidence intervals from evaluation reports
anti_rework_rules.trigger: stakeholder preference for clean point estimates
anti_rework_rules.prevention: CI computation and inclusion is non-negotiable in report template
anti_rework_rules.cost_if_violated: spurious model selection decisions based on noise within CI overlap

iteration_protocol.action: pause automated evaluation; run emergency calibration batch; inspect for judge model change or rubric drift
investigate judge prompt for ordering cues; update debiasing module; re-run affected evaluations
add length-controlled evaluation variant; update prompt to discourage length bias; re-audit with length-stratified sample
remove contaminated questions; add replacement questions from held-out reserve; document which questions removed

iteration_protocol.trigger: Elo CI width exceeds 50 points after 500 matches
iteration_protocol.action: continue match collection; investigate match distribution for category skew; do not publish ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: inter-rater kappa below 0.65 on annotation batch
iteration_protocol.action: halt annotation; convene calibration session; revise rubric with disagreement examples; re-pilot

iteration_protocol.trigger: judge score trend diverges from human ratings by >0.15
iteration_protocol.action: run full human re-calibration; inspect for Goodhart gaming pattern; consider judge rotation

iteration_protocol.trigger: safety false negative rate exceeds 2% on known harm categories
iteration_protocol.action: retrain or replace safety judge; expand red-team test suite; hold model release

iteration_protocol.trigger: self-preference delta exceeds 5% relative to cross-family baseline
iteration_protocol.action: switch to ensemble of diverse-family judges; document bias in report

iteration_protocol.trigger: evaluation pipeline fails reproducibility check (>0.1 score delta)
iteration_protocol.action: audit prompt version log; check cache validity; re-run on fixed calibration set; root-cause before proceeding

priority_rationale: Priority ordered by: (1) foundational setup (paradigm, rubric, judge selection) before any evaluation; (2) bias and integrity checks before scale; (3) human calibration before reporting; (4) specialized frameworks; (5) operational/reporting infrastructure.

validation_protocol.structural_check: all required top-level keys present and correctly typed
validation_protocol.high_risk_node_obligations: nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 must have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
validation_protocol.high_coupling_node_obligations: nodes with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 must have non-empty revisit_triggers
validation_protocol.conflict_edge_obligations: edges with signed_tension<0 must have resolution_rule
validation_protocol.priority_order_completeness: priority_order must list every node id exactly once
validation_protocol.reference_resolution: every evidence_ref, competency_question_ref, conflict_axis_ref must resolve

test_cases.input_summary: single model output, pointwise rubric, GPT-4 judge
pairwise pair with known position swap inconsistency
benchmark question in training data n-gram overlap
judge score trends diverge from human ratings over 3 cycles

evaluation_suite.regression_policy: block evaluation report if human-judge correlation drops below 0.75 or position bias swap-consistency below 0.82
